question: Should stale Discord-backed session rows be removed automatically, exposed through an operator/agent cleanup action, or folded into the broader Dashboard prune workflow?
rationale: All viable fixes mutate persistent human conversation state and must settle Discord 403/404 semantics, transcript retention, startup/network cost, and whether agents may delete sessions.

options.title: Plugin-Owned Preview Cleanup
options.body: Add a Discord-owned reachability check that previews stale candidates, revalidates before deletion, and uses `sessions.delete` lifecycle semantics for cleanup.

options.title: Dashboard Prune First
options.body: Keep agents read-only and implement the broader explicit Dashboard prune UI/API first so humans approve destructive cleanup.

options.title: Hide Without Deleting
options.body: Mark unreachable rows in listing or Dashboard output without deleting stored session state, preserving history but leaving cleanup manual.

recommendation.title: Plugin-Owned Preview Cleanup
recommendation.body: Add a Discord-owned reachability check that previews stale candidates, revalidates before deletion, and uses `sessions.delete` lifecycle semantics for cleanup.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice crosses Gateway session lifecycle, agent tool exposure, and Discord plugin boundaries where Peter Steinberger has the strongest recent history.
